source: CK-12 Middle School Math Grade 8, Section 7.5, CC-BY-NC
notes: Lesson introduces Distance Formula as application of Pythagorean Theorem. Structure: motivation story → learning objectives → derivation → formula statement → worked examples × 2 → practice exercises × 3 → real-world problem. No audio units. Video: 1 interactive animation.

units.label: Real-world motivation: the vegetable garden story
units.content_summary: Narrative hook: 8th-grade class plans a vegetable garden; Belinda proposes finding the distance from the water source to the garden center to buy the correct hose length. Establishes real-world need for distance measurement.

units.label: Learning Objectives (4 objectives)
units.content_summary: Four objectives: (1) recognize Distance Formula as application of Pythagorean Theorem; (2) find distance between two points on coordinate grid; (3) find missing coordinate given distance; (4) solve real-world problems with Distance Formula.

units.label: Derivation: right triangle on coordinate grid (diagram)
units.content_summary: Coordinate grid diagram showing two points connected by a hypotenuse, with horizontal and vertical legs drawn. Labels show (x1,y1), (x2,y2), and the legs as |x2-x1| and |y2-y1|. Demonstrates the Pythagorean Theorem connection.

units.label: Derivation: algebraic steps text
units.content_summary: Step-by-step algebraic derivation: from the right triangle, hypotenuse² = (x2-x1)² + (y2-y1)², therefore d = √[(x2-x1)² + (y2-y1)²]. Connects Pythagorean Theorem to the formula.

units.label: Distance Formula statement (text)
units.content_summary: Formal statement of the Distance Formula: D = √[(x2-x1)² + (y2-y1)²]. Defines all variables. Notes that the formula works for any two points regardless of quadrant.

units.label: Interactive animation: distance formula visualisation
units.content_summary: Interactive animation allowing students to drag two points on a coordinate plane and observe the distance formula applied dynamically. Shows the right triangle construction updating in real time.

units.label: Worked Example 1: find distance between (1,4) and (5,7) — problem
units.content_summary: Coordinate grid showing points A(1,4) and B(5,7) with a line segment between them. Problem: find the length of AB.

units.label: Worked Example 1: step-by-step solution (text)
units.content_summary: Solution: d = √[(5-1)² + (7-4)²] = √[16+9] = √25 = 5. Full working shown with substitution and simplification steps.

units.label: Worked Example 2: find missing coordinate — problem (text)
units.content_summary: Problem: distance between two points is 10. One point is (-4, 8) and x-coordinate of other point is 4. Find the missing y-coordinate. Notes that there may be two answers.

units.label: Worked Example 2: solution with two answers (text)
units.content_summary: Solution: 10 = √[(4-(-4))² + (y-8)²] → 100 = 64 + (y-8)² → (y-8)² = 36 → y-8 = ±6 → y = 14 or y = 2. Both answers verified and explained.

units.label: Practice Exercise 1: distance between point pairs (3 pairs)
units.content_summary: Three coordinate pairs to practice with: (3,2) and (7,5); (-1,-1) and (3,2); (0,0) and (4,3). Students apply formula to each pair.

units.label: Practice Exercise 2: town map real-world (image)
units.content_summary: Map of Bryan's town on a coordinate grid with locations including pet store, town hall, library, school. Students find distances between pairs of locations using the Distance Formula.

units.label: Practice Exercise 3: missing y-coordinate problems (text)
units.content_summary: Three problems requiring students to find missing coordinates given two points and a distance. Emphasizes that some problems have two valid answers.

units.label: Lesson Closure: garden problem solution (text)
units.content_summary: Returns to the opening garden story. Applies Distance Formula to find the distance from the water source to the garden center, concluding the narrative and demonstrating real-world application.
